title: Database Credentials Coding Policy
summary: This policy establishes requirements for the secure storage, retrieval, and management of database authentication credentials used by software applications accessing production databases. It aims to prevent unauthorized access and reduce the risk of credential compromise by specifying secure coding and operational practices.
scope: This policy is directed at all system implementers and/or software engineers who may be coding applications that will access a production database server on the <Company Name> Network. It applies to all software (programs, modules, libraries or APIs) that will access a <Company Name>, multi-user production database. It is recommended that similar requirements be in place for non-production servers and lab environments.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - General
requirements.text: Access by software programs must be granted only after authentication with credentials.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - General
requirements.text: The credentials used for this authentication must not reside in the main, executing body of the program's source code in clear text.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - General
requirements.text: Database credentials must not be stored in a location that can be accessed through a web server.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Database user names and passwords may be stored in a file separate from the executing body of the program's code.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: This file must not be world readable or writeable.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Database credentials may reside on the database server.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: A hash function number identifying the credentials may be stored in the executing body of the program's code if credentials reside on the database server.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Database credentials may be stored as part of an authentication server (i.e., an entitlement directory), such as an LDAP server used for user authentication.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Database authentication may occur on behalf of a program as part of the user authentication process at the authentication server.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Database credentials may not reside in the documents tree of a web server.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Pass through authentication (i.e., Oracle OPS$ authentication) must not allow access to the database based solely upon a remote user's authentication on the remote host.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Storage of Data Base User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Passwords or pass phrases used to access a database must adhere to the Password Policy.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Retrieval of Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: If stored in a file that is not source code, then database user names and passwords must be read from the file immediately prior to use.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Retrieval of Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Immediately following database authentication, the memory containing the user name and password must be released or cleared.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Retrieval of Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: The scope into which you may store database credentials must be physically separated from the other areas of your code, e.g., the credentials must be in a separate source file.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Retrieval of Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: The file that contains the credentials must contain no other code but the credentials (i.e., the user name and password) and any functions, routines, or methods that will be used to access the credentials.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Retrieval of Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: For languages that execute from source code, the credentials' source file must not reside in the same browseable or executable file directory tree in which the executing body of code resides.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Access to Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Every program or every collection of programs implementing a single business function must have unique database credentials.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Access to Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Sharing of credentials between programs is not allowed.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Access to Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Database passwords used by programs are system-level passwords as defined by the Password Policy.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Access to Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: Developer groups must have a process in place to ensure that database passwords are controlled and changed in accordance with the Password Policy.

requirements.section: 4. Policy - Access to Database User Names and Passwords
requirements.text: This process must include a method for restricting knowledge of database passwords to a need-to-know basis.
